summary.text: A 49-year-old Caucasian man had a 25-year history of fixed lateral patellar dislocation of the right knee after slipping and striking the knee on the floor. He presented with right knee pain for 8 months that gradually increased and was relieved by rest, antalgic gait and the knee giving way while walking.

Examination showed anterior thigh muscle atrophy, a laterally dislocated patella, knee motion of 0-120° and a positive patellar apprehension test with negative drawer, patellar tap, joint line tenderness and Lachman tests. Radiographs showed lateral dislocation on the skyline view, no deformity, sclerosis, patella alta or baja, and a relatively normal trochlear groove, and he was diagnosed with chronic fixed lateral patellar dislocation of the right knee.

He underwent extensive lateral release, including the lateral capsule and vastus fascia, until the patella could be reduced, followed by right MPFL reconstruction with a semitendinosus graft. The graft was fixed with an endobutton on the patella and ETHIBOND suture anchored to a cancellous screw and washer on the femur, and a confirmation X-ray followed closure. A knee brace in full extension was used for up to three weeks.

At 5-year follow-up he did not complain of pain, instability or giving way, and no redislocation of the right knee was seen; no stiffness was found during five years of follow-up. He could stand and walk normally without walking aids and sit with a flexed knee without complaint. The authors described the outcome as satisfactory despite the extensive release.

ambiguities.issue: Knee flexion angle at graft fixation: the case discussion states the graft was secured with the knee flexed 30°, and later that the optimal 60° angle of knee flexion for MPFL graft fixation "was also performed in this patient"; the patellar drilling is separately stated at 60°. Parent ruling: the source does not identify the two statements as the same fixation step (the 60° sentence sits in the patellar endobutton paragraph), so this is an ambiguity, not a source conflict; both angle statements are review_only.
